Clean and merge flusurvey data tables

Source: R/merge_data.r
merge_data.Rd

Clean and merge flusurvey data tables

Usage

merge_data(
  data,
  clean = c("remove.first", "remove.bad.symptom.dates", "remove.bad.health.scores",
    "limit.season", "remove.postcodes", "n.reports", "unsuccessful.join",
    "only.symptoms"),
  min.reports = 3,
  ranges = "sample",
  age.breaks = c(18, 44, 64),
  ili.sudden.unknown = NA
)

Arguments

data

the data to merge and clean, usually the result of read_data. The surveys are joined in a fixed order (background, contact, symptom), regardless of their order in data. The last one present drives a rolling join. The result has one row per report of that survey (the symptom reports, if present), each taking the latest report of the other surveys on or before its date. When an earlier survey has several reports on the same day, its last report is used. Any other survey name gives an error.

Joining the contact and symptom surveys gives a warning. The join pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report, however long before it was filed, and a contact report describes one day whereas a symptom report describes the week before it. With 'unsuccessful.join' the symptom reports without an earlier contact report are dropped, shortening episodes of illness. To link the two, extract the symptom and contact surveys separately, get the episodes with bouts_of_illness and flag the contact reports made during an episode with flag_ill_contacts.

clean

cleaning options, NULL for no cleaning, otherwise a vector of cleans to perform (by default all): - 'remove.first', whether to remove reports from the first reporting day, - 'remove.bad.symptom.dates', whether to remove bad symptom dates: symptom start before date of first or end after end of last report, end of symptoms before start of symptoms, symptoms reported to have started or ended after date of report - 'remove.bad.health.scores', whether to remove health scores <0 or >100 - 'limit.season', whether to limit a flu season to November -> April - 'remove.postcodes', whether to remove postcodes - 'n.reports', whether to exclude those with fewer than min.reports symptom reporting days - 'unsuccessful.join', whether to exclude those with unsuccesful joins (e.g. if symptoms are reported without a background survey present; the web site should have prevented this, but doesn't appear to have done so) - 'only.symptoms', whether to exclude those that have no report without symptoms

min.reports

minimum number of symptom reporting days per user (ignored if 'min.reports' is not given as a cleaning option)

ranges

what to do if a number of contacts is given as a range: sample from the range ("sample"), or apply a function, given as character string (e.g., "mean")

age.breaks

a vector of the highest age (in whole years) in each age group except the last (first age group starts at 0 years of age). The last group is open-ended. The default gives the groups 0-18, 19-44, 45-64 and 65+, matching the age bands of the contact questions.

ili.sudden.unknown

how to interpret reports where sudden onset is unknown, passed to aggregate_symptoms: NA (the default) leaves ili and ili.fever missing where onset is needed to decide, 1 counts unknown onset as sudden and 0 as not sudden. The recorded onset is kept in onset.

Value

a rolling-joined data table. day.of.week (1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday) is that of the report date. If the contact survey is included, contact.date is the day the contacts describe (the day before the report) and contact.day.of.week is its day of the week. Use these rather than day.of.week when analysing contacts.

Author

seb

Examples

dt <- merge_data(simulated_data[["2013"]])
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use flag_ill_contacts().
table(dt$ili)
#> 
#>    f    t 
#> 2792   43 

## only remove each participant's first reporting day
merge_data(simulated_data[["2013"]], clean = "remove.first")
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use flag_ill_contacts().
